reasoning: Recent Iowa Senate polling from the last 45 days shows a very close race, with Emerson College/Nexstar giving Ashley Hinson a small lead and aggregate trackers still placing the contest in the low single digits. I could not find any current-cycle Iowa presidential poll from the last 45 days that specifically measures Iowa’s electorate for the 2026 general election, so the answer is based on Senate polling plus Iowa’s structural lean.

sources.name: Emerson College / Nexstar Media poll (reported by CBS2 Iowa)
sources.details: Emerson College/Nexstar found Ashley Hinson at 47.5% and Josh Turek at 45.0% among 712 likely voters, with 6.1% undecided and 1.4% for someone else.

sources.name: The Hill report on Emerson College / Nexstar poll
sources.details: The Hill reported the same Emerson College/Nexstar survey showing Hinson ahead of Turek 48% to 45% in the Iowa Senate race.

sources.name: PollsMax Iowa Senate polling average
sources.details: PollsMax’s Iowa Senate average shows 45.1% for the Democrat and 48.0% for the Republican, for an aggregate Republican lead of 2.9 points.

sources.name: PollsMax Iowa Senate forecast
sources.details: PollsMax forecast page shows a slightly larger Republican polling average lead of 3.6 points, using nine polls in the average.
